model: REIT distributable income capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.share_count_basis: ESTIMATED ~7,900m units: 7,611.3m in issue at 31 Dec 2025 (FY2025 FS line 1245) + ~270m from the April 2026 private placement (>=S$600m at ~S$2.2) + ~20m management-fee units through 1H 2026. The 1H 2026 interim is not in Extracted/, so this must be replaced by the 30 Jun 2026 units-in-issue figure when it is. Held FLAT thereafter: management fees paid in units are charged in the flow as the SBC-equivalent, so also counting those units as dilution would double-count. Acquisition-funding placements are treated as roughly DPU-neutral, with their accretion carried in per-unit growth.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 FS line 715: 'Management fees paid/payable in units' 52,812k (S$'000). This is the REIT analogue of SBC: distributable income adds it back as non-cash, but it is paid by issuing units to the manager. Charged in the flow via sbc_pct_path.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is the COST OF EQUITY, not WACC, because distributable income is already after interest. SGD build: 10y SGS ~2.2%, ERP 5.5%, REIT beta ~0.8 -> 6.6%, plus ~0.4% for 38.6% aggregate leverage / 26% floating-rate debt / 4.0-yr average term to maturity = 7.0% base. Bull 6.5%, bear 7.75%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lessee lease liabilities are immaterial (~S$27m); no lease adjustment. Rental income from tenants is the revenue line.
inputs.nci_treatment: Distributable income is the amount attributable to CICT unitholders (NCI in 79RR LLP 30% and Gallileo/MAC 5.1% already excluded), so no NCI deduction.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT distributable-income capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine (routing table row 'REIT / property trust'). Mapping: revenue = gross revenue; 'EBITDA margin' = distributable income / gross revenue (DI includes JV distributions, e.g. ION Orchard 50%, that sit outside gross revenue, so the margin is DI margin, not NPI margin); D&A 0; cash tax 0 (tax transparency; DI is already after tax); 'SBC' = management fees paid in units; 'capex' = a SUSTAINING capex charge (~4% of gross revenue, ~0.25% of S$27.4bn property value) that DI does not deduct; net debt held at ZERO because the flow is post-interest - subtracting the S$9.99bn borrowings would deduct debt twice. Reported borrowings S$9,989.5m and cash S$149.5m (31 Dec 2025) are kept only as memo fields. BASIS: post-merger FY2021-FY2025 only. CMT (pure retail, pre-Nov 2020) and CICT (retail + office + integrated) are different businesses; FY2015-FY2020 are legacy context and excluded from CAGRs. GAAP net income/EPS are dominated by fair-value revaluations and are not used. ANCHORS: FY2025 DI S$860.9m, DPU 11.58c; 2H25 DI S$449.0m / DPU 5.96c annualises to ~S$898m / 11.9c and still has CapitaSpring for only ~4 of 6 months. FY2026 base DI ~S$913m (DPU ~12.0c) = full-year CapitaSpring + lower cost of debt (3.2% vs 3.6%) less the Bukit Panjang Plaza divestment (S$428m, announced Feb 2026). 1H 2026 UPDATE (from Analysis.json, sourced from the 12 Aug 2026 results; that interim is NOT in Extracted/ and has not been verified against the filing): 1H26 gross revenue S$846.8m (+7.5%), DPU 6.02c (+7.1%), aggregate leverage 37.4%, cost of debt 2.9%. Paragon acquired Jul 2026 (S$3.9bn, ~3.9% yield) and Asia Square Tower 2 sale (~S$2.5bn, ~3% exit yield) agreed, guided ~2.1% DPU-accretive; funded partly by an Apr 2026 placement. Base FY2026 is therefore revenue ~S$1.75bn (+8%) and DPU ~12.2c (DI ~S$960m on ~7.9bn units); FY2027 carries the full-year net reconstitution (+4.5%) at a slightly lower DI margin (54.3%, because Paragon is debt-funded at a lower entry yield). Balance-sheet anchors stay 31 Dec 2025 because net debt does not enter this model; the share count is estimated (see share_count_basis). No numeric guidance is given by S-REIT managers.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: DPU 4-yr post-merger CAGR (FY2021 10.40c -> FY2025 11.58c). Per-unit is the right basis for a REIT that grows by issuing units.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Total equity (5.0%) and DI (7.0%) 3-yr CAGRs are inflated by unit placements funding ION Orchard (Oct 2024) and CapitaSpring (Aug 2025); per-unit DPU grew 3.1% and NAV per unit only 0.3%. Equity CAGR diverges >30% from per-unit growth and is NOT used.
historical_growth.notes: 5-yr CAGRs set null: they span the Nov 2020 CMT/CCT merger (units 3.69bn -> 6.47bn) and are not a growth trend. EPS CAGRs null: IAS 40 revaluation noise. fcf_3yr_cagr is distributable income (FY2022 702.4 -> FY2025 860.9), the REIT-relevant cash flow; fees-in-units grew roughly in line (47.8 -> 52.8) so the owner-adjusted series grows at a similar ~7%.

base.narrative: FY2026 gross revenue ~S$1.75bn (1H26 S$846.8m; full-year CapitaSpring and Gallileo, Paragon from Jul 2026, less Bukit Panjang Plaza) and DPU ~12.2c; FY2027 gets the full-year Paragon-for-AST2 swap (~2.1% DPU-accretive). After that, Singapore retail and office reversions, 96.9% occupancy and the Hougang/Tampines/Lot One/Capital Tower projects support ~3% top-line growth fading to 2%. DI margin about 54.3%: cost of debt at 2.9% helps, but 26% floating debt and refinancing over a 4-year average maturity give that back over time.

bull.narrative: Rates stay low and refinancing is accretive; Singapore core office supply stays tight and retail reversions persist in the mid-single digits; Hougang Central delivers its >5% entry yield from ~2029 and BPP proceeds are recycled accretively.

bear.narrative: Office demand softens (hybrid work, new CBD supply), reversions turn flat, Frankfurt/Sydney assets drag; cost of debt reprices back toward 3.8-4% as the 74% fixed book rolls, compressing DI margin by ~2.5pts; higher AEI spend needed to keep malls competitive.

scenario_narratives.base: Singapore-centric (94% of value) retail/office/integrated portfolio compounding per-unit distributions at ~2.5-3% early, fading to 2%, with flat DI margin and a sustaining-capex and fees-in-units charge. Value is roughly NAV (S$2.09 adjusted NAV, Dec 2025).
scenario_narratives.bull: Lower-for-longer SGD rates plus continued positive reversions and accretive redevelopment lift DPU growth toward 3.5% and the DI margin by 1.5pts; the market pays ~20x owner distributable income at exit.
scenario_narratives.bear: Office softness and debt repricing hold top-line growth at 1-1.5% while the DI margin falls ~2.5pts; a higher cost of equity and a 15x exit cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25. A diversified, investment-grade, Singapore-centric S-REIT with 38.6% leverage and staggered maturities has no solvency tail, but rate direction is genuinely two-sided, so neither tail is favoured.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Capitalise what unitholders actually receive: distributable income (post-interest, post-tax, attributable to unitholders) less the management fees paid in units (a real dilution cost DI adds back) and less a sustaining-capex charge DI does not deduct, discounted at the SGD cost of equity with net debt held at zero. Cross-check against adjusted NAV per unit (S$2.09, 31 Dec 2025) and the ~5% distribution yield.
key_risks_to_valuation: Interest rates: 26% floating debt and a 4.0-yr average maturity; each +50bp on the full S$10bn book is ~S$50m, ~6% of DI.
Office exposure (Singapore CBD supply, Frankfurt Gallileo/MAC, Sydney) - occupancy 95.7% vs retail 98.7%.
Acquisition-led growth funded by placements: per-unit accretion depends on placement price vs NAV.
Sustaining-capex charge (4% of revenue) is an estimate; disclosed capex (S$285m FY2025) mixes AEIs with maintenance.
1H 2026 figures and the post-placement unit count come from Analysis.json, not an extracted filing; the Asia Square Tower 2 sale must still complete for the ~2.1% accretion.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 2.20-2.57
data_sources.financials: CICT FY2021-FY2025 annual financial statements, FY2025 results news release (6 Feb 2026) and FY2025 results presentation in research/C38U.SI/Extracted; Metrics.csv / kpis (DistributableIncome, DPU, NAVPerShare, Gearing, CostOfDebt, Occupancy).
data_sources.qualitative: C38U.SI_Analysis.json (2026-10-24; carries the 1H 2026 results, Paragon/AST2 reconstitution and Apr 2026 placement), plus the FY2025 news release and presentation.
